recentItems.title: Container ships and oil tankers seen in Gulf of Aden as tensions rise in Yemen
recentItems.description:
(19 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Buraiqeh, Aden - 19 September 2026
1. Wide of vessels seen from the coast of Buraiqeh district in Aden, people swimming
2. Various of ships 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
At sea, in Gulf of Aden - 19 September 2026
3. Moving shot from a small boat heading towards vessels in the Gulf of Aden
4. Various of vessels in Gulf of Aden
5. Close-up on a vessel in Gulf of Aden carrying containers  
STORYLINE:
Ships were seen in the Gulf of Aden, off the Yemeni coast on Saturday as tensions in the country between Houthi rebels and Saudi backed forces rise.

It's been over a week since Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels stormed down the Red Sea coast, extending their reach to a key maritime chokepoint -Bab el-Mandeb Strait- and threatening Saudi Arabia's oil exports.

Container ships and oil tankers continued to transit the Strait after the Houthi rebels said they are only targeting Saudi-linked vessels. But a dip in traffic has been reported over the last week after a lightning advance by Houthis on islands in the waterway.

Many shipping companies abandoned the route after Houthi attacks on Israeli-linked vessels began in 2023, though vessels from Russia and China appear to have no trouble.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said his government is considering expanding the operations of a naval unit deployed in the Gulf of Aden off the coasts of Yemen and Somalia to protect his country’s vessels and oil shipping routes.

AP video by Abdulnasser Alseddik

recentItems.title: Crowds rush into Munich festival grounds as Oktoberfest opens
recentItems.description:
(19 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Munich, Germany - 19 September 2026
1. Various of people waiting in line for Oktoberfest to open
2. SOUNDBITE (German) Oskar Morgenstern, Oktoberfest visitor:
"We've been here since 2. That's 2 a.m." 
(Journalist asking: "And what have you been doing the whole time until now?") Oskar Morgenstern: "Drinking!"
3. Morgenstern and friends shouting (German/Bavarian) " One, two, drink up!"
4. SOUNDBITE (German) Oskar Morgenstern, Oktoberfest visitor:
"We'll run, we'll jump onto the next best table, and then we'll keep going until the end."
5. Trash on the ground
6. Close of person waiting, backprint on their hoodie reading: "Think global. Drink local."
7. SOUNDBITE (German) Kira Klein, Oktoberfest visitor:
"We've been here since about 03:45 a.m., and our battle plan is: to run, to just run, to the Hacker beer tent, and then to sit upon the tables."
8. Kleinn and friends waving into camera
9. SOUNDBITE (German) Kira Klein, Oktoberfest visitor:
"And then, starting at 12, the first mug of beer, and then one every hour, I'd say."
10. Crowd waiting behind barrier, cheering
11. Security personnel leading crowd towards entrance
12. Security personnel getting out of the way, crowd starting to run
13. Various of visitors flocking to festival grounds
14. Marstall beer tent
15. Horse figures atop Marstall beer tent
16. Close of sign reading (German) "Welcome to Oktoberfest"
17. Wide of Oktoberfest entrance
STORYLINE:
Hours before the gates opened, Oktoberfest visitors were already lining up for Munich’s biggest party of the year. 

Some had been waiting since the middle of the night – and had clearly come with a plan.

As soon as security cleared the way, the crowd cheered and made a beeline for the beer tents, with some visitors breaking into a run to grab a table.

The world’s largest beer festival is expected to draw millions of visitors over the coming weeks. 

A liter of beer costs an average of 15.61 euros this year, up 2.4% from 2025.

AP video by: Philipp-Moritz Jenne

recentItems.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread farther and longer
recentItems.description:
(19 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rome - 18 September 2026
1. Close of “Laboratories — Medical Entomology” sign, at the ISS (Istituto Superiore di Sanita — Italian Superior Institute for Health) and researcher walking though door 
2. Various mosquito larvae in baskets 
3. Various of researchers taking mosquitos’ box from a storage box with controlled temperature and mixing it with new larvae to make tests 
4. Mosquitos flying inside cage 
5. Computer screen showing latest data regularly collected by the ISS on the spreading of mosquito-born deceases, including West Nile virus  
6. Various of Antonino Bella, researcher at Italy’s National Institute of Health checking the data on the computer 
7. Close of screen showing Italy’s map divided by administrative regions and showing in red those regions (19 out of 10 total regions) where cases have been reported 
8. SOUNDBITE (Italian) Antonino Bella, researcher at ISS (Italy’s National Institute of Health):
"As we know, the climate changes, especially high temperatures, affect for two reasons essentially: one, they favor the proliferation of mosquitoes, there is a favorable condition for the mosquito to reproduce, and also they also extend the season and therefore the possibility that there will be the presence of the infected mosquito that can in turn infect humans. So the number of cases may also increase due to the extension of the season in which we observe the cases. As we said, the West disease is now endemic in Italy and usually the season starts in June and generally ends in October but there were seasons in which we found cases even at the beginning of November.”
9. Various of mosquitoes’ larvae in boxes with water 
STORYLINE:
Italian health authorities say rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across wider areas and for more months of the year.

More than 650 infections have been reported in Italy so far this year, accounting for roughly half of all cases recorded in Europe, according to local health authorities.

Antonino Bella, researcher at Italy’s National Institute of Health, or ISS, said that higher temperatures because of climate change "help mosquitoes reproduce" and "extend the transmission season".

Scientists are not sounding the alarm, West Nile virus has been considered endemic in Italy since 2020, when cases began to surge, and infections are now reported each summer and into early fall.

About 80% of infected people develop no symptoms, while most others experience a mild flu-like illness.

Severe neurological complications occur in a small minority of cases, mainly among older adults and people with underlying health conditions.

Experts say this year’s case numbers are broadly in line with recent seasons.

Areas once largely unaffected are increasingly reporting infections, reflecting a gradual expansion of the virus across the country.

Italy’s experience with the virus is drawing attention from European countries located farther north. 

A Belgian research team visited the ISS last May to study Italy’s research and surveillance system after the country began recording locally acquired West Nile cases.

The Netherlands this year has reported more than two dozen West Nile cases, the first since 2020, as well as several deaths, according to its public health institute.


The Aedes aegypti — known to transmit dengue, yellow fever, chikungunya, zika and West Nile viruses — has been established in Cyprus since 2022 and may spread to other European countries.




AP Video by Andrea Rosa

recentItems.title: Polls open in Moscow for the second day of Russia's parliamentary election
recentItems.description:
(19 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++PLEASE NOTE: AP IS OPERATING IN RUSSIA ACCORDING TO RUSSIAN RESTRICTIONS ON ALL REPORTING RELATED TO THE ONGOING MILITARY OPERATION IN UKRAINE++

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Moscow, Russia - 19 September 2026
1. Polling station workers listening to national anthem
2. Close up of people applauding, Roman Sukhov, chairperson of the precinct election commission speaking UPSOUND (Russian): 
"Dear colleagues, our polling station is open for the second day of voting. I wish all my colleagues, as well as the observers, who are also practically becoming colleagues, a good, calm day."
3. Wide of polling station interior
4. Various of man receiving ballot papers and walking to voting booth
5. Man casting ballot
6. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Emma Kuznetsova (89), pensioner, Moscow resident:
"I hope (the election brings) a positive mood to the entire nation. I hope the war ends as soon as possible. And may God grant that everyone finds happiness and well-being on this earth."
7. Mid of voting machines 
8. Mid of polling station workers
9. Woman voting 
10. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Maria Kazakova (33), Moscow resident:
"I came here out of a sense of duty. I expect (from the election) a degree of reasonableness, much like most of us do, I suppose. And, fundamentally, safety above all. That is always the top priority for me, my safety and the safety of my family."
11. Various of man receiving ballot papers and voting
12. Various of woman receiving ballot papers and voting

STORYLINE:
Polls opened in Moscow on Saturday for the second day of voting in the country’s parliamentary election.

Authorities spread the election out over the weekend in a bid to boost turnout among the 111 million eligible voters and even allowed electronic balloting. 

Polls opened across Russia’s 11 timezones on Friday and will end on Sunday.

Voters cast two separate ballots, filling half of the State Duma’s 450 seats by selecting political parties listed on the ballot. The rest are contested in single-seat constituencies, with voters choosing individual candidates.

United Russia, the main Kremlin party, is expected to keep its grip on the State Duma alongside a few other parties.

recentItems.title: Doctors treat those injured in a powerful bomb blast at a mosque in northwestern Pakistan
recentItems.description:
(19 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kohat, Pakistan - 19 September 2026
1. Various of those injured in blast undergoing treatment at the District Headquarters Hospital, Kohat
2.SOUNDBITE (Urdu) Umar Hayat (ASI) Assistant Sub-Inspector police :
"The prayer was scheduled for around 1:15 p.m. We had just reached the second rak'ah when a powerful explosion occurred. I lost consciousness as a wall collapsed on top of me, and I was unaware of anything that happened afterward. When I regained consciousness, I found myself in this hospital." 
3. Various of Khayal Zaman receiving treatment 
4. SOUNDBITE: (Urdu) Khayal Zaman, Police constable:
"When we went for prayers, the congregation had already started. As we went into sajdah, a sudden explosion took place and the roof collapsed on us. We remained trapped under the rubble for a long time before people managed to pull us out. There were a lot of people there, and the place was extremely crowded."
5. Various of injured 
6. Various of hospital's exterior
STORYLINE:
Pakistani security forces ended on Saturday a standoff with militants holed up inside a police compound in northwestern Pakistan, officials said. 

The confrontation began Friday after a suicide bomber rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into a mosque, and gunmen stormed the facility, killing 21 people and wounding 103 others.

The coordinated attack occurred at a compound in Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, which borders Afghanistan. 

Many of the casualties were police officers and people attending prayers at a mosque.

Several militants took up positions inside the complex, and a shootout with security officers ensued, police official Mohammad Sadiq said. 

The complex houses the police's Special Branch intelligence agency, offices of the Counter Terrorism Department, and houses of counterterrorism officers who have carried out operations against militants across the province in recent years.

Sadiq said the operation ended after 20 hours. 

Security forces were searching the compound and nearby areas, and the bodies of eight attackers were recovered, according to local police. 

Bursts of gunfire could be heard in the compound as additional security personnel arrived, residents said, before the operation ended.

Sadiq said two attackers detonated explosives inside the compound Saturday morning and that police had killed six assailants so far, not including the bombers. 

It was unclear whether the new explosions caused additional casualties or how many militants remained inside.

The suicide attack on Friday brought down an outer wall of the police offices and badly damaged the mosque.

Funeral prayers for police officers killed in the assault were held late Friday at the police lines in Kohat, and their bodies, and those of killed civilians, were returned to their families for burial, Sadiq said.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the assault, but suspicion was likely to fall on the Pakistani Taliban, formally known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, which has intensified attacks on police and other security forces in recent years.

The TTP is separate from but allied with Afghanistan’s Taliban, which returned to power in 2021. 

Pakistan frequently accuses the Taliban government in Kabul of sheltering TTP leaders and allowing militants to carry out cross-border attacks. Afghanistan’s government denies the allegations.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack in separate statements and expressed sorrow over the deaths. 



AP video shot by Maaz Awan

recentItems.title: Funeral held for those killed in bombing at mosque near police offices in Pakistan
recentItems.description:
(19 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province - 19 September 2026
1. Various shots of funeral prayers being offered for the victims of yesterday's bomb blast
2. SOUNDBITE: (Pashto) Khurshid Khan, brother of victim:
"Both in the police force and at home, he always emphasized good conduct and respect for others. We never saw him lose his temper and spent many wonderful moments with him. We only pray that Allah grants him the highest place in Jannah and blesses him in the hereafter."
3. Various shots of the body being carried for burial
4. SOUNDBITE (Pashto) Azmat Ullah, relative of victim:
"The police department includes people from all walks of life, but he was a truly kind and respectable man. He never caused the slightest trouble to anyone in the neighborhood. He leaves behind three daughters and an only son, a young boy who is still in the sixth grade. The responsibility of the entire family has now fallen on his shoulders.There is little we can say except that it was God's will. May Allah grant him the highest place in Jannah and give his family the strength and patience to bear this immense loss."
5. Various shots of people burying the deceased
6. Various shots of military security deployed in the area
7. Wide shot of military helicopter conducting security patrols over the area
STORYLINE:
A vehicle bomb exploded Friday at a mosque near police offices in northwestern Pakistan as gunmen tried to storm the compound in an attack that killed at least 21 people and wounded 80 others, police and rescue officials said. Among those killed and wounded were police officers attending prayers at the mosque.

The coordinated assault was the latest in a surge of militant violence near the border with Afghanistan where Pakistani Taliban militants have increasingly targeted police and other security forces as the government intensifies operations against them.

The bombing occurred in Kohat, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. An attacker apparently rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the mosque, said Zulfiqar Hameed, the provincial police chief.

At least seven armed gunmen also attempted to enter the police compound and exchanged fire with officers. Six of the gunmen were killed, according to police, who said one suicide bomber attacked the nearby office of an intelligence agency.

The police compound housed counter-terrorism police, who had carried out operations against militants across the province in recent years.

Most of those killed were police officers, hospital officials said. Bilal Faizi, a senior rescue official, said most of the dead and wounded had been attending prayers at the mosque.

Photos from the scene showed the outer wall of the police offices had collapsed and the mosque was badly damaged. Smoke rose over the site after the blast, which witnesses and residents said was heard far away, followed by gunfire. Inside the mosque, piles of bricks and concrete buried the floor, wires dangled from cracked walls and daylight poured through jagged holes in the roof, while a ceiling fan hung above the wreckage.

Residents said the exchange of fire continued hours after the coordinated attack.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack and expressed sorrow over the casualties. He directed authorities to accelerate rescue operations.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack, but suspicion was likely to fall on the Pakistani Taliban, formally known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP.






AP video by Maaz Awan
Production by Muhammad Yousaf

recentItems.title: Taiwan launches international alliance for disaster management
recentItems.description:
(19 Sep 2026) 
RESTRCITION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Taipei City - 19 September 2026
1. Various of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te on stage with founding member countries of the World Alliance for Disaster Management (WADM) for a photo session 
2. Various of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te arriving on stage 
3. SOUNDBITE (Mandarin), Lai Ching-te, Taiwan President:
“When authoritarianism intends to instill terror, democratic societies must emanate confidence through resilience. When authoritarianism intends to divide unity, democratic partners must join hands to work together. Peace comes through strength, strength comes through resilience, resilience comes through unity. All our preparations aim at defending the people’s welfare and preserve their freedom and democratic ways of life, defend peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region and the rest of the world. Meanwhile, facing the increasingly unpredictable climatic changes, we aim at letting the society having more capacities to respond to conflicts, to recover quickly and to be sustainable.” 
4. Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey getting on stage 
5. SOUNDBITE (English), Palmer Luckey, Anduril Industries founder:
“Your soldiers are increasingly practicing mission command and learning to act independently from the top all the way down to the bottom. A force that knows how to improvise and that has the freedom and ability to act. It is practice on how to improvise and how to be flexible that has an enormous advantage over a micro-managed force that has to ask permission for everything they do, whose weapons necessarily require that permission.”
6. Various of Taiwan President in a group photo with Palmer Luckey 
7. SOUNDBITE (English), Palmer Luckey, Anduril Industries founder:
“I also want to argue that Taiwan will not be able to build a proper industrial base around Taiwan’s domestic demand alone. Taiwan already makes the best air soft guns in the world. Whether it’s the largest producers or the smallest shops, the quality is trusted around the world and the supply is omni present. Even the Japanese market is flooded with Taiwanese craftsmanship when it comes to the toy air soft gun space. And that’s great. But it’s representing a missed commercial opportunity. Don’t just sell air soft guns. Make real guns. Sell them to the countries that share Taiwan’s commitment to freedom, and make those countries depend on you for advanced capabilities the way the world already depends on TSMC for commercial capabilities." 
8. Various of Taiwan National Security Council Secretary General Joseph Wu (man with glasses and dark red necktie) interacting with guests 
9. Various of Taiwan defense minister Wellington Koo (man with glasses and dark grey necktie) interacting with guests 
10. Various of logo of World Alliance for Disaster Management (WADM) 
STORYLINE:
Taiwan has formally launched World Alliance for Disaster Management (WADM), an international alliance that gathers the capabilities of 11 countries to strengthen cooperation on disaster preparedness and response Saturday morning.  

The WADM aims at bringing together governments, emergency response agencies, businesses, academic institutions and civil society groups to cooperate throughout the disaster management cycle. 

Speaking at the launching ceremony of the WADM, Taiwan President Lai Ching-te said that when authoritarianism intends to instill terror, "democratic societies must emanate confidence through resilience." 




The alliance includes 12 founding members and 21 observers. 

AP video shot by Taijing Wu.

STORYLINE:
Grammy-winning American singer Chappell Roan was among the attendees at the Ludovic de Saint Sernin Fall/Winter 2025-2026 fashion show in Paris Saturday. 

Saint Sernin, considered part of the "new queer wave" in fashion, presented an unapologetically sexy collection true to form.

Crossing gender conventions, the collection featured figure hugging tailoring, midriff baring ensembles, latex, studs and snake print.

The color palette was muted - black, grey, brown and beige dominated, but were accented by pops of red and white.

In addition to Roan, other attendees at the show included Argentine-Spanish model Georgina Rodríguez and Argentine singer and actress Tini.

13. SOUNDBITE (Portuguese) Denise Barros, teacher: 
"There is no better president than Lula when it comes to social programs. He is the best president and brought social programs to many areas, especially education"
14. Various of crowd singing a famous Lula campaign song at the ending of the event
STORYLINE:
Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva held a campaign rally in the city of Guarulhos, São Paulo, mobilizing voters in a key state a few weeks before the voting. 

During the event, he said he wants to end the operation of online betting companies in Brazil, citing the social impact of gambling.

"This idea that getting rid of betting companies will destroy football is a lie. We are going to put an end to these betting companies—we are going to put an end to money laundering," he said responding to a criticism from football clubs.

Lula also defended maintaining social programs implemented by previous Workers' Party governments, including the Bolsa Família welfare program.

The president criticized presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro during the rally, as the two candidates are close on the polls ahead of the October 4th first-round election.

The event was attended by political allies including Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and former ministers Fernando Haddad and Marina Silva.

STORYLINE:
Lily James, Mingyu and Cristin Milioti were among the stars in attendance at Dior's fall 2025 show in Paris.

Inside the venue the past and present collided in a dreamlike spectacle, where Maria Grazia Chiuri riffed on ruffs — both literally and literarily.

Inspired by Orlando, Virginia Woolf’s time- and gender-traveling protagonist, the ready-to-wear collection spun historical silhouettes into a vision of fluid, ever-evolving femininity. If this is indeed one of Chiuri’s last collections, as rumors suggest, she’s leaving on a high.

Cause where I come from you are judged for what you do."

"Really, really amazing, we loved it, we loved the characters, the costumes, the fact that the cast is South African, it was like wonderful. She actually wants to come back tomorrow."
7. Mid of performers in elaborate costumes on stage
8. Mid of audience member recording a performance on their phone
9. SOUNDBITE (English) Zenzele Letsoela, Professional dancer: 
++SOUNDBITE PARTLY COVERED BY SHOTS 10, 11, 12++
"I've gotten so many comments since me and Brian are literally the only people of colour in most of the productions, people are like, are you guys sure that you are people of colour and someone would literally ask like to touch our skins to make sure that it's not like, like paint or like makeup and like was like it it's not, it's very rare to see a person of colour doing this kind of, of performing."
10. Mid of performers in elaborate costumes 
11. Mid of performers in elaborate costumes on stage performing
12. Wide of performers on stage with vibrant lighting 
13. Wide of performers in elaborate costumes on stage
STORYLINE:
Clutching an aerial hoop on a Johannesburg circus stage, a young performer pauses for a split second before launching into the air and gliding, drawing cheers from the crowd below.

For 29-year-old Brian Ngobese, who grew up in South Africa’s impoverished Alexandra township, moments like this mean more than applause. The circus has given him a stage, a livelihood, and a way to turn his talent into work.

“Before the circus, it was mostly dance, education, being an influential purpose in my baby brother's life, but once the circus life started, I was more than happy to show who I am, who I can be without being scared, who I'm supposed to be without being judged by other people outside," said Ngobese. "Cause where I come from you are judged for what you do." 

Ngobese’s older brother first introduced him to South African street and social dancing. He later moved into contemporary, hip-hop and other styles, building on a love of performing that began in childhood.

He found circus almost by accident after auditioning as a dancer for a Joburg Theatre production in 2019. What began as a short job became a career when The Cirk invited him to stay and train.

Ngobese received support for training and transportation through Jozi Circus School’s youth development program. The school partners with The Cirk, where he now works.

Behind the colorful spectacle is a social program that helps performers from under-resourced communities turn talent into opportunity and paid work.


The program is designed to sustain itself through training, performances and other circus work rather than relying entirely on outside funding.
